milestones.title: M0 - Product Truth Cleanup
milestones.description:
## Outcome
Make user-visible defaults, CLI help, CI behavior, and release metadata tell the same verified truth.

## Exit gate
- #211 and #212 are implemented on `main`.
- Generated workflows and the root Action share explicit advisory/blocking semantics.
- Help, Action, docs, and CLI contract tests are green.

milestones.title: M1 - First-Run Excellence
milestones.description:
## Outcome
A new user can install, scan, understand the verdict, and take the correct next action without seeing a false clean.

## Exit gate
- Packaged first-run, unsupported, partial, and richer-findings paths have executable coverage.
- Trust states and next actions are consistent across terminal, JSON, PR, and docs.
- Demo and empty-state assets cannot drift silently.

milestones.title: M2 - Safe CI Adoption
milestones.description:
## Outcome
CI adoption is advisory-first, explicit when enforcing, and safe for repositories with existing debt.

## Exit gate
- Advisory is the install default; blocking requires an explicit gate.
- Baseline creation, comparison, pruning, expiry, and ownership are defined.
- PR feedback is concise, idempotent, and covered by advisory/explicit-blocking states.

milestones.title: M15 - Telemetry & Product Analytics
milestones.description:
## Outcome
Telemetry remains a deliberate, privacy-reviewed product decision; activation never depends on collection.

## Exit gate
- #274 explicitly chooses no-collect, opt-in, or another bounded policy.
- Threat model, consent, retention, deletion, redaction, and alternatives are approved.
- Any implementation has inspect/send/first-run controls and privacy regression tests.

milestones.title: M17 - Release
milestones.description:
## Outcome
Release readiness uses one auditable product-quality and maintainer go/no-go record.

## Exit gate
- Required M0–M17 exit evidence and owners are current.
- Scorecards, proof, comparison, lifecycle, and claim gates use canonical current issues.
- Pricing, cohorts, and telemetry do not silently block zero-config activation.

milestones.title: M16 - External Validation
milestones.description:
## Outcome
External claims are backed by consent, pinned inputs, public methods, and reproducible evidence.

## Exit gate
- Cohort, benchmark, gallery, and feedback work records provenance and limitations.
- No external result blocks a release without consent and an evidence owner.
- Internal fixtures never masquerade as external validation.

milestones.title: M3 - Trust Engine Hardening
milestones.description:
## Outcome
Rule health is measured, explainable, certifiable, and resistant to gaming or unjustified promotion.

## Exit gate
- Core rules have reproducible TP/FP/UNSURE replay and calibration evidence.
- Lifecycle transitions require fixture, owner, revision, and rollback evidence.
- FP adjudication and trust-score contributions are structured and auditable.

milestones.title: M4 - Verification Intelligence Expansion
milestones.description:
## Outcome
Verification explanations are honest about unknown, partial, stale, and unsupported evidence across supported languages and CI providers.

## Exit gate
- The false-green taxonomy and lifecycle/action/assertion contracts are executable.
- At least one semantic mechanism works end-to-end with hostile and runtime evidence.
- CI integrity uses provider-aware parsing and never converts an unfinished scan into clean.

milestones.title: M5 - Framework Excellence
milestones.description:
## Outcome
Framework and CI capability claims are generated from evidence, per-capability maturity, fixtures, and limitations.

## Exit gate
- One canonical capability registry drives docs and drift checks.
- Playwright, Jest/Vitest, and pytest have semantic/runtime certification evidence.
- Supported CI providers share a generated parity matrix; unsupported analysis remains explicitly marked.

milestones.title: M6 - Suppression / Policy / Governance
milestones.description:
## Outcome
Suppressions and local policy changes are explicit, expiring, auditable, and cannot hide regressions or false-green results.

## Exit gate
- Governance evaluates all-tier pre-suppression findings and matched suppression counts.
- Identity, expiry, renewal, owner, scope, and total-count limits are enforced.
- Baseline, terminal, JSON, SARIF, and PR outputs preserve suppression provenance.

milestones.title: M7 - Performance & Determinism
milestones.description:
## Outcome
Performance and determinism claims are backed by frozen corpora, reproducible budgets, and fail-safe cache/incremental behavior.

## Exit gate
- Small, medium, monorepo, and pathological tiers have cross-platform evidence.
- Wall/CPU/RSS/first-run budgets and regressions are machine-checked.
- Full/incremental outputs are equivalent and cache invalidation is diagnosable.

milestones.title: M8 - Security & Hostile Repository Model
milestones.description:
## Outcome
Untrusted repositories, configs, plugins, and artifacts cannot execute code or escape scan boundaries by default.

## Exit gate
- The threat model maps assets, boundaries, adversaries, controls, and tests.
- Traversal, resource-budget, hostile-input, artifact, and plugin edge cases are explicit.
- A vulnerability-response drill produces tracked corrective actions.

milestones.title: M9 - Public Contracts & Migration
milestones.description:
## Outcome
Public schemas, commands, artifacts, rule IDs, deprecations, and migrations are versioned and upgrade-safe.

## Exit gate
- The contract registry is complete, owned, and release-validated.
- Current and prior fixtures prove compatibility for every frozen artifact.
- Breaking-change budgets, doctor/migration behavior, and release-note links are enforced.

milestones.title: M10 - Monorepo & Incremental Correctness
milestones.description:
## Outcome
Monorepo and incremental analysis preserve complete, typed, and deterministic repository state.

## Exit gate
- Multi-root/workspace/package/framework discovery and generated/vendor policy are explicit.
- Changed scope expands through dependencies, helpers, config, and tests.
- Partial states, CI topology, exit codes, and report projections share one status contract.

milestones.title: M11 - Extensibility & API
milestones.description:
## Outcome
The canonical engine API and local extension surface are versioned, trust-scoped, and testable without new abstractions.

## Exit gate
- Custom rule authors can version and test a pack against one stable contract.
- Unsafe packs cannot gain stronger trust or silent execution privileges.
- Compatibility/deprecation and contribution rules are documented and tested.

milestones.title: M12 - Forensics & Historical Trust
milestones.description:
## Outcome
Forensics, provenance, confidence, and history explain why a result exists and how it changes over time.

## Exit gate
- Root-cause, evidence freshness, contradiction, and confidence states are explicit.
- One trust diff composes score, suppression, and false-green movement.
- Evidence graph/history use the canonical identity and remain local/deterministic.

milestones.title: M13 - Supply Chain & Release Integrity
milestones.description:
## Outcome
Release provenance, rollback, canary, and dependency updates are reproducible, drillable, and enforced.

## Exit gate
- Two clean builds produce equivalent package evidence.
- Candidate-versus-current canary and rollback/kill-switch drills are executable.
- Dependencies have owners, SLAs, exceptions, and emergency patch evidence.

milestones.title: M14 - Enterprise Governance & Developer Experience
milestones.description:
## Outcome
Local configuration, governance, diagnostics, ownership, compatibility, and maintainer operations are explicit and verifiable.

## Exit gate
- Config explain/verify and policy inheritance/exception behavior are tested.
- Doctor, architecture, ownership, ADR, test, and debt standards are maintained.
- Support, accessibility, compatibility, and distribution claims are honest.

milestones.title: M18 - Post-MVP Activation and Verified Adoption
milestones.description:
## Outcome
Release readiness uses one auditable product-quality and maintainer go/no-go record.

## Exit gate
- Required M0–M17 exit evidence and owners are current.
- Scorecards, proof, comparison, lifecycle, and claim gates use canonical current issues.
- Pricing, cohorts, and telemetry do not silently block zero-config activation.

milestones.title: M19 - Scalable Deterministic Analysis Engine
milestones.description:
## Outcome
Scale work adds measured scheduling, cache, equivalence, and fault isolation without weakening determinism.

## Exit gate
- A local modular-runtime ADR, cancellable scheduler, and 10k/100k/1m evidence exist.
- Cache, monorepo, equivalence, and fault work remain in their canonical M7/M10 issues.
- Remote protocol, hosted workers, and cross-repository exchange are not local prerequisites.

milestones.title: M20 - Universal Language Trust Program
milestones.description:
## Outcome
A rolling language-certification program promotes only evidence-backed capabilities; no universal-support claim exists.

## Exit gate
- Candidate intake and feasibility are decided through M16 external validation.
- Per-language certification uses the canonical adapter, lifecycle, measurement, and support contracts.
- First and future cohorts are independent; future cohorts cannot block current correctness.

milestones.title: M21 - Evidence Graph and Runtime Verification Intelligence
milestones.description:
## Outcome
The local evidence graph has an approved identity/storage/export architecture and deterministic query projections.

## Exit gate
- #575 records storage, identity, migration, and export boundaries.
- Graph materialization, runtime freshness, cache recovery, and APIs extend current M4/M7/M12 issues.
- Hosted exchange and future language cohorts are not graph-program prerequisites.

milestones.title: M22 - Verified Agentic Remediation Loop
milestones.description:
## Outcome
A proposed future remediation loop remains bounded to dry-run/PR-first, sandboxed, receipted, human-approved changes.

## Exit gate
- Tool authority, sandbox, receipts, and human approval are approved before writes.
- Adversarial agent regressions are executable and independent.
- BYOM, generic language placeholders, hosted control planes, and release claims are excluded.

milestones.title: M23 - Team Trust Control Plane
milestones.description:
## Outcome
Decide whether a hosted team-trust topology should exist; do not build a control plane before that decision.

## Exit gate
- #602 records service boundary, trust domain, tenancy, data, offline, and operating-cost alternatives.
- A named owner and approved demand/packaging evidence are required before implementation issues reopen.
- Current milestone contains discovery/ADR work only.

milestones.title: M24 - Enterprise Assurance and Sovereign Operation
milestones.description:
## Outcome
Decide whether an enterprise assurance offer is justified and bound its threat/data flows before implementation.

## Exit gate
- #617 documents enterprise-specific assets, adversaries, trust boundaries, and controls.
- A supported customer/topology and named owner are required before SSO, CMK, pilots, or compliance automation reopen.
- Current milestone contains intake/architecture decisions only.

milestones.title: M25 - Ecosystem and Verification Intelligence
milestones.description:
## Outcome

A public, reproducible ecosystem turns Mjölnir trust data into better verification decisions, integrations, custom standards, and measurable product leadership.

## Entry gate

- M20 through M24 trust, scale, agent, control-plane, and enterprise contracts are stable.

## Exit gate

- Third parties can reproduce benchmarks and build safe extensions.
- Ecosystem artifacts are signed and auditable.
- Adoption is measured through verified release decisions and retained teams.
- Quality guardrails improve rather than trade away determinism.
- Language throughput remains measurable and the next frontier is activated without a blanket coverage claim.
- Commercial packaging is validated with customers.

## Dependencies

- [M20-01](https://github.com/Sergey-Bar/Mjolnir/issues/561)
- [M21-01](https://github.com/Sergey-Bar/Mjolnir/issues/574)
- [M22-01](https://github.com/Sergey-Bar/Mjolnir/issues/587)
- [M23-01](https://github.com/Sergey-Bar/Mjolnir/issues/601)
- [M24-01](https://github.com/Sergey-Bar/Mjolnir/issues/616)

## Non-goals

- Do not promise market leadership, universal language support, or a guaranteed commercial outcome.
- Do not let probabilistic, model-generated, or third-party output silently change a blocking verdict.
- Do not retain raw source by default or make hosted intelligence a prerequisite for local verification.
- Do not use commercial packaging, translations, or case studies as dark patterns or unsupported claims.
- Do not turn the rolling language program into a fixed end-state promise.

## Tracking issue

[M25-01 — Track ecosystem and verification intelligence](https://github.com/Sergey-Bar/Mjolnir/issues/632)
